    Attempted function name — Scientific layout

    AC10

    Expression before typing "s", "i", "n":

    0.5+

    After typing "s", "i", "n": still "0.5+" — unchanged. Only tapping the on-screen "sin(" button inserts that token.

    Pending team confirmation

    The work item leaves open whether typing a full scientific function name on the keyboard (e.g. literally typing "s", "i", "n", "(") should act as a shortcut for the on-screen "sin(" button. This design's default is no: letter keys are never mapped in either layout (AC8–AC10), so typing "sin(" has no effect and the function must be inserted by tapping its button.

    If the team confirms typed function names should work, the only change needed here is adding a small keyword-matching layer in the Scientific layout's keydown handler (watching for "sin(", "cos(", "log(", etc. as they're typed) — the key map, display, and error states in this design would not need to change.
